title: Hypotheses of Brown representability
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\neq\ell$, and let $X$ be a separated scheme of finite type over $k$ in the standing setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside it, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$. Let $\Lambda$ be one of $A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, where $A$ is a finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$, with the condensed coefficient structures of [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Then $\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$ is locally small and triangulated, has arbitrary direct sums, and has split idempotents. The thick [pur9-def-thick] category $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ is essentially small, and a small skeleton (any one) is a set of compact generators of $\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$: each of its objects is compact in $\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$ [def-pc-compact-object], and the family generates $\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$ [def-pc-generators].

proof.text: Fix the standing datum $(p,\ell,k)$ and a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], and fix one of the displayed admissible coefficient rings $\Lambda$. The coefficient list, condensed topologies, pulled-back ring object $\Lambda_X$, unbounded module-object ambient category $\mathcal T=D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$, constructible finite-Tor subcategory $\mathcal S=\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$, replete localizing intersection, and fixed small indexing universe are exactly those specified by [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Put $\mathcal L=\Loc(\mathcal S)$. All direct sums below use this fixed universe; no derived-completeness condition is added.

source.place: item statement and proof first paragraph; standing scheme setting and localizing-closure definitions

proof.text: Apply [det-brown-hypotheses-ambient] to this finite-type standing scheme and admissible $\Lambda$: $\mathcal L=\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$ is locally small and triangulated, has arbitrary direct sums, and has split idempotents. Apply [det-brown-hypotheses-small] under the same hypotheses: $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ is thick and essentially small. Choose one representative of each isomorphism class in this essentially small category; their full subcategory is a small skeleton, so small skeletons exist. Let $G$ be any small skeleton of $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$.

Apply [det-brown-hypotheses-generation] to this finite-type standing scheme, admissible $\Lambda$, and small skeleton $G$. Every object of $G$ is compact in $\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$. Moreover, for every $K\in\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$, if $\Hom(C[n],K)=0$ for every $C\in G$ and every $n\in\mathbf Z$, then $K=0$. The first clause is compactness of each object of $G$ in the sense of [def-pc-compact-object]. For the second, $\mathcal L$ has direct sums, and $\Hom(\bigoplus_{C\in G}C,K[-n])=\prod_{C\in G}\Hom(C[n],K)$ for every $n\in\mathbf Z$; so every nonzero $K\in\mathcal L$ admits an integer $n$ and a nonzero morphism $\bigoplus_{C\in G}C\to K[-n]$, i.e. the family $G$ generates $\mathcal L$ in the sense of [def-pc-generators]. Since the standing datum and $\Lambda$ were arbitrary, the conclusions hold throughout the stated range.
